question: Should QQBot intentionally fail closed at 16 MiB for inbound gateway messages, accepting disconnects for any legitimate QQ event above that ceiling?
rationale: The implementation and transport behavior are clear, but QQ’s published event-envelope material cited in the PR does not establish a maximum production event size; only an owner can choose the acceptable delivery-versus-resource-bound trade-off.

options.title: Accept the 16 MiB ceiling
options.body: Merge the plugin-local limit as a deliberate operational policy, retaining the existing test and loopback proof.

options.title: Choose a QQ-backed ceiling
options.body: Ask for QQ gateway documentation or production evidence that supports a different fixed bound, then update the constant and proof accordingly.

options.title: Keep the current dependency default
options.body: Close or pause the PR if maintainers do not want a fixed fail-closed receive policy for QQBot.

recommendation.title: Accept the 16 MiB ceiling
recommendation.body: Merge the plugin-local limit as a deliberate operational policy, retaining the existing test and loopback proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history places this person on the QQBot gateway connection factory and its transport-lifecycle tests.
